expo.name: Huddle
expo.//backgroundColor: Soft Minimal's `colors.screen`, retained as the native/loading fallback while the full-viewport TV background image resolves. Stated here so the native window is already right before any React view exists — otherwise a cold start flashes the platform default before the native splash and animated boot surface take over. Kept honest by color-literals.test.ts, which is also why the value is written out: Expo transpiles app.config.ts and then requires it, so importing the token is not possible.
expo.//splash: The expo-splash-screen plugin below is the native source of truth. Expo 57 still accepts the legacy top-level splash field but prebuild ignores it and emits the grey target-grid placeholder, so the plugin is intentional and verified from generated Android resources.

ios.//infoPlist: CALayer.allowsEdgeAntialiasing is false by default, and a layer carrying a transform is composited without antialiasing — so Soft Minimal's ±1–2° sticker tilts turn every tile border into a visible staircase (measured: a rotated edge steps 2px per 50 rows with no intermediate pixel values, where Android feathers the same edge). This key turns edge antialiasing on app-wide. Apple documents a rendering cost; the TV screens are near-static, so it does not matter here. Only the TV app needs it — nothing in the Controller is rotated.

expo.//icon: Reaches outside the app directory into packages/ui/assets, which is where runtime artwork lives for both apps. Expo resolves this relative to the app directory and Metro's watchFolders already cover the workspace, so the path holds — but it is the kind of thing a `prebuild` proves rather than a reader.
